DNP-DGL is a tolerogenic B cell mitogen that causes B cells to become unresponsive to the same hapten, DNP, when presented on a different carrier, DNP-FL.
the copolymer D-GL can induce tolerance to DNP in B cells in vitro.

In summary, our research is concerned with
a possible mechanism for induction of B cell unresponsiveness in the mouse, namely, by coupling of a hapten, DNP, to a synthetic copolymer of amino acids (DNP-DGL), which is a B cell mitogen.
the study of the mechanism of B cell tolerance in vitro.
the study of the induction of B cell tolerance by DNP coupled to D-GL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DNP-DGL is a B cell tolerogen.
DNP-D-Gl is a tolerogen for B lymphocytes, that the mechanism of action is probably direct, and that this tolerogenic effect is independent of the presence of T lymphocytes.
DNP-D-Gl can induce unresponsiveness in vitro to DNP in both CBA and nude spleen cells, but that the latter population is less responsive to the immunogen than are cells from CBA mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNP-DGL is a B cell tolerogen in vivo and in vitro and is effective at concentrations of 1 µg or less.
DNP-DGL is a potent tolerogen, and is capable of tolerizing B cells in vitro.
DNP-DGL, a T-independent antigen, can induce B cell unresponsiveness to T-dependent antigens, and that the mechanism of this unresponsiveness is probably the same as that of T-dependent antigens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the B cells are the cells that are tolerized to DNP-D- GL.
the DNP-D- GL tolerogenic response is not dependent upon the presence of thymus-derived lymphocytes.
the DNP-D- GL tolerogen can be used to generate unresponsiveness in vitro in B cells from both normal mice as well as from mice lacking a thymus.
